sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Grayson County, KY?
sections.html:
The Grayson County Sheriff's Office collects the bill, and the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value. The sheriff works from 117 S. Main Street in Leitchfield, KY 42754, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Central Time, at (270) 259-3024. The sheriff's own FAQ sends questions about assessed value and exemptions to the PVA at (270) 259-4838.

Bills that go unpaid move to a third office. Once a real property bill is transferred, the Grayson County Clerk at (270) 259-5295 gives payoff figures. Keep these three numbers together if you are preparing a house for sale, because a buyer's title company will ask which office holds each year's bill.

  • Pay a current bill online through the sheriff's portal, by mail or at the office. Credit cards work online and at the counter, and a processing fee applies.
  • The sheriff takes the full bill only. Installments and partial payments are refused.
  • If a bill has not reached you by November 10, call the sheriff for a duplicate and have the property address and owner name ready.
  • If a lender escrows your taxes, forward the bill to the lender and check later that it was paid.

sections.h2: What is Grayson County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Grayson County is a mostly rural county in west central Kentucky with Leitchfield as its seat and largest city. It was formed in 1810 from parts of Hardin and Ohio counties and covers about 497 square miles of land. Caneyville and Clarkson are the other two cities, and Big Clifty is a census-designated place.

Two Army Corps of Engineers lakes shape the local market. Rough River Lake sits on the northern border and Nolin River Lake on the southeast edge, and local businesses use the name "Twin Lakes" because of them. The Western Kentucky Parkway and US 62 carry most traffic, and the county has its own airport. The 2020 census counted 13,275 housing units, with 21.4 percent of them vacant in a county with lake property and farmland.

The Census Bureau's county table for Grayson gives this picture:

  • Population estimate for July 2025: 27,406, up 3.7 percent from the April 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 74.6 percent, across 10,129 households.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes (2020 to 2024): $164,600.
  • Median gross rent: $658. Median household income: $50,757. Persons in poverty: 22.4 percent.

For a house that needs repairs or carries back taxes, a buyer who pays cash and takes the property as it stands can close without waiting on repairs or a lender appraisal.

sections.h2: When are 2026 Grayson County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
For 2026 bills the sheriff's schedule gives a discount period from November 1 to November 30, 2026, face amount through December 31, and penalties from January 1, 2027. Kentucky's general rule in KRS 134.015 is a 2 percent discount for full payment by November 1, no penalty through December 31, 5 percent in January and 10 percent after that. Grayson's sheriff publishes its own windows, listed in the table below.

sections.h2: What are fire and rescue dues on a Grayson County bill?
sections.html:
Fire and rescue dues are a membership charge for the county's fire districts that appears on the same bill as the property tax. An owner can remove it for one year with a signed opt-out form, and the form has to travel with the payment. The sheriff asks owners to call the office before paying online if they plan to opt out.

The form carries a warning that matters to anyone selling or holding a vacant house. Under KRS 75.450, an owner who opts out can be charged by the fire district a minimum of $500 or $1,000, depending on the type of facility, if a fire or other non-medical incident happens on the property. The opt-out lasts for the year of the form only, so a new one is needed each year.

If you are listing a house, decide on the dues before the bill is paid, and tell the closing agent what was done.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Grayson County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the Grayson County PVA, because Kentucky does not allow an appeal without one. The tax roll is open for inspection for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, and conferences run during that window and earlier once notices go out. Call (270) 259-4838 to set a time.

  • At the conference the PVA must explain how your value was reached and keep a written record of what you claimed and what was agreed.
  • File the appeal with the county clerk by the close of business on the workday after the inspection period ends.
  • The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring construction costs, insurance records, photos of defects and local sale listings, because the board denies appeals with no documents.
  • Skip the hearing and you lose the next step, an appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

Paid representatives must be on the state's approved list, which includes attorneys, CPAs and licensed appraisers, and they need written authority from you. If bills are printed before the appeal ends and the final value comes out higher than you claimed, the clerk issues a supplemental bill for the difference.

sections.h2: Does Grayson County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or totally disabled and who live in the home. The Department of Revenue sets the exemption at $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, and it comes off the assessed value before tax is figured. A house assessed at Grayson's Census median of $164,600 would be taxed on $115,500.

The application goes to the Grayson County PVA with proof of age, such as a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Owners who qualify through disability must have been classified as totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program and must reapply every year, unless they are a veteran with a service-connected disability or have been found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

After a sale, ask the PVA what to file so the exemption comes off the house you sold and can be claimed at your next home.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Grayson County house with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax follows the parcel. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and the lien from a delinquent bill lasts until it is paid or 11 years pass under KRS 134.420, whoever owns the house. A title search will turn it up.

After the April 15 transfer, 1 percent interest is added for each month, the clerk and county attorney add commissions, and a lien fee is charged. The county attorney mails a first notice within 30 days and a second within 60 days. A tax sale is set 90 to 135 days after the transfer, and a third party can buy the certificate and add its own charges to what you owe.

Before you list, ask the sheriff for a payoff on the current year and the clerk for any transferred bills. Those totals are normally paid out of the sale proceeds at closing, which is how an owner with several years behind can still sell.

faqs.q: What is the last day for the 2% discount on 2026 Grayson County bills?
faqs.a: November 30, 2026. The sheriff's schedule gives the discount for payment between November 1 and November 30, then the face amount through December 31, 2026. Penalties begin January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: Can I pay Grayson County property tax in installments?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff's office takes the whole bill and does not accept installments or partial payments. A lender that escrows your taxes can pay the full amount on your behalf.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Grayson County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff at (270) 259-3024 if the bill has not come by November 10 and ask for a duplicate. Have the property address and the owner's name available.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Grayson County bill after April 15?
faqs.a: At the Grayson County Clerk's office. Unpaid real property bills are transferred there after April 15, and the clerk, reachable at (270) 259-5295, can give the payoff with interest and commissions.

faqs.q: Who handles the homestead exemption in Grayson County?
faqs.a: The Grayson County PVA, at (270) 259-4838. Applications are filed there with proof of age or disability, and the 2025 and 2026 exemption is $49,100 off assessed value.
